request.spec:
A DRAFT claim may have lines: a label, a quantity (a whole number, at least 1) and a unit amount
(two decimals), added from the claim (CLAIM_LINE_ADDED naming the claim with its new amount, ending
label=<label> qty=<qty> unit=<unit>). With lines, the claim's amount is the quantities times the
unit amounts added up, and an edit that types another amount is refused; a line on a claim that is
not a DRAFT, in a closed period, or locked by another user is refused. Show the lines on the claim as
<label> <qty> x <unit>. Adding a line counts as editing the claim.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A DRAFT claim may have lines: a label, a quantity (a whole number, at least 1) and a unit amount
(two decimals), added from the claim (CLAIM_LINE_ADDED naming the claim with its new amount, ending
label=<label> qty=<qty> unit=<unit>). With lines, the claim's amount is the quantities times the
unit amounts added up, and an edit that types another amount is refused; a line on a claim that is

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Claim lines are in, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec: the main "claim lines" test and its three scenarios.

**How it behaves**
- Each claim row now has a label, quantity and unit amount field and an "Add line" button. Lines show on the claim as `<label> <qty> x <unit>`, in the order they were added.
- Once a claim has lines, its amount is always the quantities times the unit amounts added up. An edit, or the in-row amount save, that types a different amount is refused with its own error message. Saving the same amount (for example, an edit that only changes the note) still goes through.
- A line is refused, and nothing is written, if:
  - the label is blank;
  - the quantity isn't a whole number of at least 1;
  - the unit amount has more than two decimals;
  - the claim isn't a DRAFT;
  - the claim is due inside a closed period;
  - another user's editor has the claim locked.
- Adding a line counts as editing: it records the user as the claim's last editor. It writes `CLAIM_LINE_ADDED … person=… amount=<new amount> date=… label=… qty=… unit=…` to the audit file.

**What changed**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V78__claim_line.sql`, adds a `claim_line` table. It is set up the same way as the existing claim comments.
- **Server:**
  - A new `ClaimLine` type is attached to `Claim`, which works out the amount from its lines.
  - `ClaimService.addLine` adds a line.
  - `edit` now has the check that refuses a different amount.
  - There is a new endpoint, `POST /claims/{id}/lines`, and claims sent to the screen now include their `lines`.
  - A different amount is refused with a conflict (409) of its own type, `lined-amount`, so the screen can tell it apart from "not editable".
- **Front end:** `claims.ts` has the list of lines, the add-line fields and the new error messages.

Two cases I left alone:
- **Copying a sheet:** lines are not copied to the new sheet, just as comments aren't today.
- **Split:** I didn't add any handling for lines there. Split only applies to OPEN claims, and lines can only be added to DRAFT ones, so it shouldn't come up.
